card.name: Linking words before opioid drug names
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as in, of, as and for that come right before an opioid drug name or the word opioid(s) in opioid label text. The next word is expected to be a drug like hydrocodone, oxycodone or fentanyl.

modes.label: In/as before a combination product
modes.description: The word in or as sits just before a named opioid combination product.
modes.example: MAOIs or tricyclic antidepressants with hydrocodone, one of the active ingredients<< in>> Hydrocodone Bitartrate and

modes.label: Of/for before opioid class terms
modes.description: The word of or for comes before opioid analgesics or a specific opioid in warnings and risk statements.
modes.example: Advise pregnant women using opioids<< for>> an extended period of time of the risk

card.writes: It seems to push the next word toward a drug-name start and away from words like consume.
card.plain: It fires on the small connecting word just before an opioid name is expected in a label.
